description: getNextNonce()'s approval-settlement (ensureApprovalsSettled) determines which spender to approve by fetching a SEPARATE, small fixed-size 'probe' route (APPROVAL_PROBE_AMOUNT_BASE_UNITS = 1 USDC), independent from the REAL swap route signAndBroadcast fetches later using the actual, driver-computed amount (up to $20 / SWAP_MAX_USD). Neither behavioral-spec.md nor verification-architecture.md's edge cases discuss the risk that Skip's route/operations/spender selection for a 1-USDC probe amount could differ from the selection for the real (larger) amount -- e.g. a different bridge/spender contract chosen at a different amount tier. If that happens, the approval settled at getNextNonce()-time targets the WRONG spender, and signAndBroadcast's own allowance check (which IS correctly designed to fail closed rather than attempt a second, nonce-colliding approve) will throw on every real invocation, permanently blocking this feature's only funding mechanism -- a silent, hard-to-diagnose denial-of-service that no test exercises (no test fixture ever uses two DIFFERENT routes/spenders for the probe vs. the real signAndBroadcast call).
